subject: Cohort Voucher Stacking & Hardware Credit Split for Spring Surge Program
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@bluetreevc.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: BlueTree Programs <programs@bluetreevc.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on voucher stacking + hardware split for Spring Surge

Hi Aditya,

Quick one — the Spring Surge cohort kicks off July 1 and a couple startups asked whether they can stack a Redwood cohort voucher with the standard Redwoods-for-Startups voucher (the founder voucher). Specifically: can a startup apply both a $20k cohort credit and their $5k founder credit to the same account, and if so, can those credits be split so the $20k covers dedicated GPU/hardware allocation while the $5k covers platform (API tokens/embeddings)?

Two asks from our side:
- Can Redwood approve stacking for select cohorts as a one-time exception?
- If yes, can credits be allocated across credit buckets (hardware vs platform consumption) so we can report infra usage separately back to our sponsors?

Attaching the cohort FAQ and our proposed voucher rules. Happy to jump on a quick call if easier — we have sponsor billing review next Tues.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Morales
Head, Partnerships — BlueTree Ventures
--- attachment: SPRING-SURGE-FAQ.pdf ---

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@bluetreevc.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on voucher stacking + hardware split for Spring Surge

Elena — thanks for the clear summary and the doc.

Short answer: possibly. I need to loop in Lauren (pricing) and Monica (finance/contracting) to confirm operational/contracting implications. A few items for us to check internally:

1) Policy/precedent: We have historically avoided stacking two promotional credits on one account except for explicitly-approved partner cohorts. We can consider a partner exception for BlueTree if terms and reporting are clear.

2) Accounting split: Splitting credits between hardware credits (applied to Dedicated GPU reservations) and platform credits (consumption on hosted API) is feasible but requires work from billing to create two distinct credit types and for the Console to display consumption against each. Monica — can Finance create a cohort credit type that flows to infra-invoice lines?

3) Abuse/risk controls: We should limit stacking to an allowlist of BlueTree startups and cap the number of stacked vouchers per cohort (suggest: max 50 startups). Also set expiry windows and no-refunds.

I can approve starting the operational review if pricing/legal signs off on the exception. Looping in Lauren and Monica.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 08:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on voucher stacking + hardware split for Spring Surge

On Thu, Jun 10, 2027 at 11:03 AM Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai> wrote:
> 2) Accounting split: Splitting credits between hardware credits (applied to Dedicated GPU reservations) and platform credits (consumption on hosted API) is feasible but requires work from billing to create two distinct credit types and for the Console to display consumption against each. Monica — can Finance create a cohort credit type that flows to infra-invoice lines?

Aditya — Finance can create separate credit buckets. Operational notes:
- We will need a signed MOU or rider from BlueTree confirming which startups are eligible (allowlist) and the sponsor reporting cadence.
- Finance needs a unique credit code per cohort (e.g., BT-SS-2027-CRED-01) to avoid reconciliation ambiguity.
- Hardware credits will be applied as an invoice-level adjustment to Dedicated reservations (so they reduce invoice line "GPU Reserved Capacity"). Platform credits are consumed against hosted API charges.

Constraints:
- Creating and wiring the buckets will take ~6 business days (billing + Console tagging + accounting mapping).
- We should cap the stacked amount: suggest cohort hardware credit max $20k + founder voucher $5k stacked, per startup. Anything above requires legal sign-off.

I'll prepare a short rider template and a checklist for ops if we agree.

-Monica
Monica Patel
Sr. Manager, Revenue Operations

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 10:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on voucher stacking + hardware split for Spring Surge

Thanks for the context — a couple pricing points from my side:
- We can offer a partner cohort stacking exception but need a defined metric floor to avoid heavy subsidization. Recommend: minimum committed Dedicated reservation of 2 vGPU-weeks per month for any startup that uses the hardware credit (so credits go to accounts actively running infra). This protects us from credits being issued but never consumed.
- Pricing tiers: hardware credits should map to our Standard Dedicated rates; if they want Priority clusters we should discount only the platform portion, not hardware.
- We should not change founder voucher rules; allow stacking as an exception only when BlueTree signs the partner rider and agrees to sponsor reporting.

If you give the greenlight I can draft the partner exception clause and the metric floor language.

-Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Principal Pricing Strategist

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@bluetreevc.com>, BlueTree Programs <programs@bluetreevc.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on voucher stacking + hardware split for Spring Surge — Proposal

Elena — thanks for the patience. Summary and proposed path:

1) One-time partner exception: Redwood approves stacking of the BlueTree Spring Surge cohort credit (up to $20k) with the existing founder voucher (up to $5k) for an allowlist of startups (max 50) — conditional on a signed partner rider.

2) Credit buckets: Finance will issue two credit codes per eligible account: a hardware credit code that applies to Dedicated GPU invoice lines and a platform credit code for hosted API consumption. Finance estimated ~6 business days to set up the buckets after the rider is signed.

3) Safeguards:
- Minimum committed infra usage: 2 vGPU-weeks/month to draw from hardware credits.
- Expiry: both credits expire 90 days after issuance.
- No refunds; credits are non-transferable.

4) Next steps:
- BlueTree to confirm list of startups (allowlist) and sign the partner rider (I will share the draft).
- Monica to provision credit codes once rider is executed.
- Lauren to review the rider clause for the metric floor and reporting language.

Attaching the rider draft and our FAQ. If you want a short call to finalize before Tues sponsor review we can do 30 minutes Mon morning.

Regards,
Aditya Rao
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
